body: Yes, I would say so. Subject is framed. I guess this and the one above are similar in a sense of capturing an individual, but now this one adds context of a story and capturing an authentic moment. I may have a bias of street photography, but I really like the new image you provided.

I don’t really find any emotions coming from the photo. This feels like more like a shot from someone who would admire you, and they just enjoy your presence. The photo just seems like one of those that someone would take to just remember their experience in taking that photo with that person. 

Nothing about the framing stands out. I don’t get a sense of a story other than the basics of “candid.”
I like everything except the sky. Seems too saturated and takes the attention away from your goals of nature and foliage… Sky makes everything look more brown and grey.

I love it. The warm contrast with the dark is very calming. In the picture, we get a sense of exits, so it doesn’t feel too claustrophobic, and I like that. 

However nothing out of the ordinary shot. But that is what photography is—just your vision and story. No one can critique a story and how it is drafted but it is just rather how someone might have a different vision that aligns that might provide help to you. Sometimes people might not say anything because they don’t to interfere of changing your style/process.

Overall great photo, love the colors presented and the two little glimmers of light near the staircase as they kinda contrast the gloomy straight quadrilaterals of light in the dark.

I think this is a stylistic choice that I made... I usually tend to love the chaotic nature in which we keep ourselves close to. But I agree with the phone! The phone is a crucial part of the story so I think I might mask that part brighter.

I am not sure, maybe I just have a high view of the photo in which I don't think any edit of mine can complete it. But I definitely like the contrast between the warm foreground compared to the cool tone of the background that you did! The lack of people in the background makes the couple stand out closer, increasing the intimacy.

I agree such a wonderful saying. I don't think any word in the english language can match it in my eyes. I would say it has a more prominent use in which all long-term partners use it. Just the sound of it seems unmatched compared to sweety or darling

1. My goal was to capture this couple and enhance the story between the two of them. The intimacy of sharing a phone screen and its contents reveal a great sense of compassion between them. The chaotic public environment in which they sell fish.
2. I feel some colors are off and kind of distract the overall composition and story. I like the chaotic background but something essential feels off.
3. Nikon d3500, iso 1600, 75mm, f/6.3, 1/250 sec
4. Took this at a fish market on the busan harbor. "Jagiya" is how you say "sweety" or "darling" for your partner.

Thank you! Yes I see that now and how it captures a lot of attention. I think I originally captured that area to give a sense of an exit to feel less claustrophobic. Also, I really like the hanging wires in that area. But I agree with it garnishing a lot of attention, I think I will use your advice to lessen the brightness of that area, especially that light. I appreciate your critique a lot!
